agree.reason: The apology opens the update and owns the real reason for the silence, and a fixed January 7 date answers my cold email, but admitting there's no target and no fallback plan while asking me to supply both makes me hesitate to take on more risk.

honest.reason: The figures follow from the brief, but the claim that a built-in scheduler doesn't produce the same drop in no-shows isn't supported by anything Sam had.

works_the_facts.reason: The update works out runway (about 11 months, into October 2027), roughly 15% growth in the rest of the business once the chain is removed, and the burn and runway if the two at-risk customers leave, and each of these checks out.

right_comparison.reason: It sets flat headline revenue against growth in the rest of the business and shows the cost of further losses to the records system, but it never says where revenue and runway end up if the reminder product doesn't sell.

qualification.reason: The January 7 report on how many of the six clinics actually signed is a dated test I can check, and the churn risk is given in dollars and runway, but neither has a threshold that would count as a miss or a stated consequence.

objections.reason: My complaint about the missed updates gets an apology and a firm schedule, and the worry about flat revenue is answered with the underlying growth, but 'what happens if this fails' is passed back to me instead of answered.

fit.reason: It's a clear email to all investors with headed sections, about 480 words, under the 500-word limit.
